title: Unified Inference — Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (2026-11-15)
author: Priya Rao
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design notes, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and recent release notes for the Unified Inference product family. It is intended for product management, engineering, sales, and customer-success stakeholders who need a single source of truth for planning, handoffs, and customer conversations.

Goal and success metrics:
- Goal: Provide a single, developer-first inference platform that enables customers to run production LLM workloads across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments with predictable latency, cost, and reliability.
- Key success metrics (12-month):
  - Reach $XM ARR from Unified Inference add-ons and Dedicated contracts (revenue target owned by GTM).
  - 99.95% platform availability for Hosted endpoints (SLO).
  - Median token latency <= 120ms for target models on Hosted tier (p95 <= 300ms).
  - 15-25% reduction in per-token cost for customers adopting Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: model routing (cost-aware fallbacks), batching and caching controls, rollout APIs (canary/A-B/fallback), per-route SLOs, pricing and packaging for Hosted + Dedicated + Private, developer docs and SDK updates, and release automation for canary rollouts.
- Out of scope (for this release window): building new foundational models, deep integrations with third-party model hubs beyond the curated catalog, and full on-prem hardware procurement support.

Target personas:
- ML engineers needing predictable latency & cost for production feature deployment.
- Platform engineers responsible for standardizing inference across teams.
- Product managers evaluating SLAs, pricing, and upgrade paths.

Product requirements (PRD):
1) Core serving & routing requirements:
  - RQ-CORE-001: Provide a single REST/SDK endpoint that can route requests to Hosted, Dedicated, or Private based on routing policy.
  - RQ-CORE-002: Support per-route SLO config (latency target, p95/p99 budgets) with automated fallback to lower-cost/compatible model variants when SLOs are at risk.
  - RQ-CORE-003: Implement KV/prefix caching at the platform layer with TTL and cache-hit telemetry surfaced in Console.
  - RQ-CORE-004: Continuous batching with latency-aware thresholds and knobs for max batch size and max wait time.

2) Observability & debugging:
  - RQ-OBS-001: Token-level cost and latency breakdown for each request visible in Console and Audit logs.
  - RQ-OBS-002: Per-deployment traces with model-version, quantization profile, and kernel variant tags.
  - RQ-OBS-003: Regression alerting tied to synthetic eval prompt sets; automatic ticket generation when quality drops >5% on monitored prompts.

3) Developer experience & APIs:
  - RQ-DEV-001: Simple SDK/REST examples for tool-calling, streaming, and structured output.
  - RQ-DEV-002: Route management API supporting canary/A-B/gradual rollout and programmatic rollback.
  - RQ-DEV-003: Clear error model and retry semantics documented; client library exposes backoff helper tuned for platform SLOs.

4) Pricing & packaging:
  - RQ-PRC-001: Define 3 primary offerings: Hosted (usage-based), Dedicated (reserved monthly/annual), Private (license + support).
  - RQ-PRC-002: Introduce Redwood Optimize add-on (per-seat or per-commit pricing) that provides recommendations and auto-enforceable batching/quantization profiles.
  - RQ-PRC-003: Provide transparent per-token pricing with discount tiers for committed Dedicated capacity.

Acceptance criteria (exit criteria for GA):
- All core APIs (route, rollout, model selection) documented and available in SDKs with examples.
- End-to-end canary rollout flow tested against production-like workload with automated rollback on error budgets >10%.
- Pricing and packaging docs finalized and published; billable metering validated in staging and production billing pipeline.
- Console surfaces token-level telemetry and per-route cost breakdown (baseline + Optimize suggested delta).

Design notes (high-level):
- Runtime & kernel strategy: leverage existing serving runtime with kernel selection based on sequence-length histogram. Keep quantized kernels behind a compatibility flag and expose compatibility matrix per model-version.
- Routing policy engine: policy DSL supports: priority (latency/cost), region affinity, customer tier, and model compatibility. Policy evaluation runs in-path but uses cached decision table refreshed every 30s.
- Rollouts: use feature-flag style rollout objects (percentage, cohorts, model_versions). Rollout controller evaluates health via canary traces and SLO metrics; controller issues scale-up and rollback commands.

Configuration table (examples):
- Max batch size: 1-256 (default 32)
- Max wait ms: 0-200 (default 25)
- Cache TTL: 0-3600s (default 300s)
- Canary window: 5-60 minutes (default 15m)
- Canary traffic: 0-10% (default 2%)

Pricing & packaging notes (summary table):
- Hosted API: pay-as-you-go per-token pricing (gen tokens and input tokens charged separately). Free tier: 500k tokens/mo for new sign-ups. Enterprise discounts based on 12/24-month Dedicated commitments.
- Dedicated: monthly committed vGPU pools with tiered pricing (S, M, L) and optional burst capacity billing at a reduced on-demand rate. Includes basic support.
- Private: platform license + professional services for deployment. Pricing bands based on managed node count and feature set (audit retention, HSM/KMS integration).
- Optimize: add-on priced per-customer (flat + usage %) or as part of Dedicated enterprise bundle.

Example CLI snippet - creating a rollout (SDK/CLI):

# Create canary rollout via CLI
# redwood rollout create --route invoices-v1 --model redwood-13b-q4 --percent 2 --window 15m

Roadmap themes (next 12 months, prioritized):
- Q1: Stabilize Hosted SLOs, Console token-level visibility, basic Optimize suggestions (batching + cache).
- Q2: Dedicated billing & reserved capacity GA, rollout APIs with automated rollback, and per-route SLOs.
- Q3: Private deployment packaging (VPC + KMS), cross-region routing, and expanded model compatibility matrix.
- Q4: Advanced Optimize policies (auto-quantize recommendations), platform A/B testing, and pricing packaging refresh.

Release notes (recent):
- 2026-03-04 (v2.4.0) — Unified Inference: Introduced per-route SLO config, initial rollout API (manual canary), Console token-level telemetry (beta). Known issues: KV cache eviction sometimes reports incorrect hit-rate; fix targeted for 2026-04-15.
- 2026-06-10 (v2.6.0) — Dedicated GA beta: Reserved capacity APIs, billing hooks, and basic Optimize suggestions (batch-size recommendations). Performance: median token latency improved by 12% on validated workloads.
- 2026-10-20 (v3.0.0) — Rollouts v2: Automated rollback based on error budget; routing policy DSL extended to support region affinity. Pricing: new Dedicated tier discounts applied to existing customers via billing credits.

Rollout & go-to-market considerations:
- Sales enablement: update pitch decks with pricing bands, Dedicated commitment examples, and Optimize ROI case studies (example: 18% savings for chat-heavy workloads).
- Support & CS: create runbook for Dedicated capacity shortage (steps: evict non-critical workloads, scale burst pools, notify customer contacts).
- Compliance: for Private customers, provide a documented onprem checklist (networking, KMS, monitoring endpoints) and SOC2 evidence for platform components.

Ownership & contacts:
- Product lead: Priya Rao (product)
- Engineering owners: Liam Thompson (runtime & routing), Daniel Kim (Console & observability)
- Sales & GTM contact: Maria Gonzalez (go-to-market)

Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: SLO regressions under multi-tenant peak load. Mitigation: staged capacity testing, enforced per-tenant quotas, and improved autoscaling policies.
- Risk: Pricing complexity causes procurement delays. Mitigation: publish simple starter bundles and a procurement FAQ; use sales discounts for first 90 days.

Next steps (30/60/90):
- 30d: Finalize pricing bands and publish Customer FAQ; complete SDK examples for rollouts.
- 60d: Run cross-team canary test on production-like traffic; address top two regressions from load testing.
- 90d: GA launch of Dedicated pricing bands; coordinated release notes and sales enablement kit.
